Primary care physicians in some regions, including Italy, are often underutilizing antibiotics when treating patients with peptic ulcer disease (PUD), despite being targeted appropriately by their physicians. While Italian primary care physicians have made significant efforts to address eradication therapy for H. pylori infection and provide sensitive data on community influenza activity, this focus may not be extending to non-ulcer PUD cases.

Research suggests that underprescription of antibiotics for peptic ulcer disease is a pressing issue. For instance, a prompt from the healthcare dataset indicates that primary care physicians in certain regions are not adequately using antibiotics when treating patients with PUD. This highlights an opportunity for improvement in prescribing behavior among these physicians.

In addition to direct feedback on antibiotic use, incorporating more evidence-based guidelines and monitoring of patient outcomes could also help address this issue. Furthermore, integrating antibiotic data into broader community surveillance systems may provide valuable insights that complement local data and enable better decision-making regarding antibiotic usage.
